purpose: two-track (N=2) Ardour session generation from a static template with per-track sources/instruments and a headless render; complements the conductor one-track/template-swap probe

generation.method: copy template; add second abc2midi SMF; duplicate Route/Playlist/Source XML blocks with new IDs; add interchange MIDI 2-1.mid
generation.second_abc:
X:1
T:Ardour second voice
M:4/4
L:1/4
Q:1/4=120
K:C
E G B d |
generation.lua: load_session; for each track add gmsynth; save_state("two")
generation.instrument: bundled gmsynth LV2, default program 0 on both tracks

export_log_extra: DummyMidiBuffer: it's too late for this event 226 > 176.
DummyMidiBuffer: it's too late for this event 674 > 624.
DummyMidiBuffer: it's too late for this event 98 > 48.

contribution_check.comparison: sample-wise subtraction of one-track four-gmsynth.wav from two-track two-gmsynth.wav (same first track, same gmsynth)
contribution_check.conclusion: the second generated track contributes to the master; this is a mix-level check, not stem isolation

proven: two-track session with distinct MIDI sources can be generated by deterministic XML edits from a static template
Lua can instrument both tracks and save headlessly
CLI exporter renders the generated session master headlessly
not_proven: general version-pinned session generator for arbitrary voice counts/names/programs/tempo-meter changes
headless MIDI import through a supported API
limits: hand-patched XML from an old 3001 fixture

stems.method: solo one track at a time via Lua solo_control():set_value(1/0, PBD.GroupControlDisposition.NoGroup); save stem1/stem2; render each snapshot with ardour9-export

stem1.note: byte-identical to the one-track four-note export

stems.proven: each MIDI track can be soloed, rendered separately and reconstructed into the master; per-track audio evidence exists
not_proven: batch stem export without changing solo state
